label: Cursor Performer
description: The film's protagonist hand: a cursor that travels the scene and CLICKS the thing that causes the next beat -- UI exhibits become a story someone is doing. Position its box over the whole stage at a high z_index. CONTINUITY CONTRACT: when threading the cursor across consecutive scenes, make each scene's FIRST path point equal the previous scene's LAST point (same x/y), so the hand reads as continuous through hard cuts. Use on 2-4 consecutive UI scenes max; it should always be traveling toward or clicking something meaningful. MULTIPLAYER CAST: pass `cast` instead of `path` for several NAMED cursors moving at once over a product surface -- that is a different claim, not a busier version of the same one. One hand says 'someone is doing this'; a cast says 'a team is already in here'. Spend it on a takeover or social-proof beat, with 2-4 members, and give each a real path (drifting name tags with nothing to do read as decoration).

path.label: [{at, x:'62%', y:'48%', click?:true}] -- scene-local seconds, stage-relative coords. The single protagonist hand.

cast.label: MULTIPLAYER: [{name:'Maria', color?:'#2d7ff9', path:[{at,x,y,click?}]}] -- up to 6. Names render as colored pills trailing each tip; colors auto-assign from a distinct palette when omitted. Overrides `path`.

color.label: Cursor color for the single-hand form (default near-black)

enter.label: 'fade' to fade in at the first point (default: present from start)

exit.label: 'fade' to fade out after the last point
